agent.summary: Implemented PF_DELTA in xs-rs: negotiation, destination signatures, streaming weak/strong block matching, LITERAL/COPY/DELTA_END records, retry acknowledgments, changed-basis rejection, and final XXH3-128 verification. C++ and Rust now delta in all four client/server directions, and the C++ delta wire suite passes unchanged against the Rust binary.
agent.diagnosis: This step targets wire volume rather than a timed optimization. With the frame recorder, a 4 MiB file with a 100 KiB changed region sent less than half the file as DATA in all four interop directions; before PF_DELTA the same runs send the whole file. The new receiver tests also confirm that a bad digest or changed basis publishes nothing and exits 23.
agent.change: Added rs/xs-rs/src/delta.rs (signature generation/encoding, streaming block matcher, basis verification) and wired PF_DELTA through sender NEED parsing, F_DELTA_REQUEST/signature exchange, LITERAL/COPY/DELTA_END emission, receiver signature replies, retry acks, serialized delta writes and final digest checks. Also added --ignore-times/-I and the HELLO flag so the C++ delta tests can force a transfer.
agent.expected_effect: Changed large files cross the wire as literals plus verified basis-block copies instead of full contents, while missing bases, non-regular destinations, unsupported peers and --whole-file safely fall back to normal or non-delta transfers.
agent.risks: No --inplace or --link-dest basis snapshot is needed yet because xs-rs does not implement those modes; it writes through temp files. Delta reads and writes are serialized as in C++, so per-file range parallelism does not apply during a delta attempt. The sender now sends a fatal MSG (and stderr text) on protocol errors, matching C++ instead of only exiting.
